copy_accounting.notes: Direct host fetch happens inside AsymGEMM kernels and is not counted as a Python tensor copy. Staged/Torch fallback copy bytes are zero for asym_only reports unless fallback calls are nonzero.

bubble_candidates.name: base_forward_frozen_dispatch
bubble_candidates.why_it_can_create_gpu_bubbles: CPU-resident base-weight fetch plus GEMM in forward. A high share means PCIe/NVLink fetch latency or small-M GEMM occupancy may be limiting GPU utilization.

bubble_candidates.name: base_dx_frozen_dispatch
bubble_candidates.why_it_can_create_gpu_bubbles: CPU-resident original weight fetch for dX. This now uses transpose_b=True and should not include W.T host materialization.

bubble_candidates.name: optimizer
bubble_candidates.why_it_can_create_gpu_bubbles: Optimizer update. For LoRA-only SFT this is usually small, but Python optimizer overhead can still serialize steps.

bubble_candidates.name: route_metadata
bubble_candidates.why_it_can_create_gpu_bubbles: MoE route metadata construction. CPU/PyTorch launch gaps here can leave the GPU idle before expert kernels.

bubble_candidates.name: route_scatter
bubble_candidates.why_it_can_create_gpu_bubbles: MoE output scatter/index_add. This is a common non-GEMM tail after expert compute.

bubble_candidates.name: route_pack
bubble_candidates.why_it_can_create_gpu_bubbles: MoE token gather/pack. If large, expert GEMMs wait for scattered token layout preparation.
